title: Invocation
description: An observed call into a contract. Invocations are how a runtime dependency between two contracts is established, which is why the caller is optional and the callee is not: a contract invoked directly by an account has an identifiable callee but no contract caller, and recording a fabricated caller for that case would create a dependency that does not exist.

caller.description: The contract that made the call, when the call was made by a contract rather than by an account or by the transaction itself. Absent means the caller was not a contract or was not observable.

callerAccount.description: The account that originated the invocation chain, when the call originated from an account. Recorded only as an observation; not used as evidence of ownership.

function.description: The invoked function name, when it could be recovered from the invocation details. Absent means the function could not be determined, which is common for calls made through a host function whose arguments are not exposed as a named invocation.

transactionHash.description: The transaction whose execution performed this invocation.

operationIndex.description: The operation within the transaction that triggered this invocation.

callDepth.description: The nesting depth of this invocation within its transaction, with 1 for a direct call. Recorded so that a reader can tell a direct dependency from one several frames deep without re-deriving the call tree.

successful.description: Whether the invocation completed successfully, where the network record makes it determinable.

argumentsDigest.description: A digest over the invocation arguments, without recording the arguments themselves. This lets two invocations be compared for equality without Amasario retaining potentially sensitive payloads.

returnDigest.description: A digest over the returned value, where recording the value itself is undesirable.

events.description: Event identifiers emitted by the callee during this invocation.
